title: Split-family strictification with a compatible coherent map
statement:
Use categories in the sense of [def-nagata-category] and universes of [def-weil-size-convention], enlarged to contain all the families below. Let $J$ be a small category. A normalized covariant category-valued pseudofunctor $P$ assigns a category $P(j)$ to each object, a functor $P(a):P(j)\to P(k)$ to each $a:j\to k$, and natural isomorphisms $\mu_{b,a}:P(b)P(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}P(ba)$. Require $P(1)=1$, identity comparisons when either arrow is an identity, and
$$\mu_{c,ba}\circ P(c)(\mu_{b,a})=\mu_{cb,a}\circ(\mu_{c,b}P(a)).$$
Let $H:J\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be a strict functor. Suppose functors $\alpha_j:H(j)\to P(j)$ have natural isomorphisms $\theta_a:P(a)\alpha_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\alpha_k H(a)$, identity at identities, satisfying
$$\theta_{ba}\circ(\mu_{b,a}\alpha_j)=(\theta_b H(a))\circ P(b)(\theta_a).$$
Here a strict functor preserves identities and composition by equality, and an equivalence of categories is a functor with a quasi-inverse and inverse natural isomorphisms.

Define $\widetilde P(j)$ to have objects families $X_a\in P(k)$ for every arrow $a:j\to k$, with isomorphisms $\gamma_{b,a}:P(b)X_a\xrightarrow{\sim}X_{ba}$ for each composable $b$, satisfying $\gamma_{1,a}=1$ and
$$\gamma_{c,ba}\circ P(c)(\gamma_{b,a})=\gamma_{cb,a}\circ\mu_{c,b}(X_a).$$
A morphism $X\to Y$ is a family $t_a:X_a\to Y_a$ with $t_{ba}\gamma^X_{b,a}=\gamma^Y_{b,a}P(b)(t_a)$. Evaluation $E_j(X)=X_{1_j}$ is an equivalence of categories, and reindexing $X_a\mapsto X_{aa_0}$ along $a_0:j\to j_1$ makes $\widetilde P$ a strict functor on $J$. There are coherent natural isomorphisms $\kappa_a:P(a)E_j\xrightarrow{\sim}E_k\widetilde P(a)$ with components $\gamma_{a,1_j}$. The formulas
$$\widetilde\alpha_j(z)_a=\alpha_k(H(a)z),\qquad \gamma_{b,a}=\theta_b(H(a)z)$$
(and the same formula on morphisms) define a strictly natural transformation $\widetilde\alpha:H\to\widetilde P$, with $E_j\widetilde\alpha_j=\alpha_j$; its comparison along $a$ under $\kappa_a$ is $\theta_a$.

More precisely, let $v:I\to J$ be a functor for which $P\circ v$ is strict, all its $\mu$ are identities, and $\alpha\circ v$ is strictly natural with all its $\theta$ identities. There is a strict functor $K:I\to\mathsf{Cat}$, a natural transformation $H\circ v\to K$, and strictly natural functors
$$\widetilde P\circ v\longleftarrow K\longrightarrow P\circ v$$
which are objectwise equivalences. Their composites on $H\circ v$ are respectively $\widetilde\alpha\circ v$ and $\alpha\circ v$. Thus the comparison also holds for diagrams equipped with these specified maps, not only object by object.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, lines 7747-7802: splitting a fibred category, dualized for covariant diagrams. The statement specifies the split-family model and compatibility with a given coherent map and strict restrictions. Compare Toën, The homotopy theory of dg-categories and derived Morita theory, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, Section 4, printed pp. 21-22, the standard rectification paragraph immediately before Sublemma 4.6. That PDF was read online and is absent locally.

proof.text: Give $\widetilde P(j)$ componentwise identities and composition. If $t:X\to Y$ and $s:Y\to Z$, their defining equations give $(s_{ba}t_{ba})\gamma^X_{b,a}=s_{ba}\gamma^Y_{b,a}P(b)t_a=\gamma^Z_{b,a}P(b)(s_at_a)$, so the composite is again a morphism. The identity equation and category laws hold componentwise by [def-nagata-category]. Evaluation at $1_j$ preserves these operations. The smallness of $J$ and the enlargement explicitly allowed in the statement put these families and their morphisms in the chosen universes [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 1 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text: For $T\in P(j)$ put $(R_jT)_a=P(a)T$ and $\gamma^{R_jT}_{b,a}=\mu_{b,a,T}$; put $(R_ju)_a=P(a)u$. The family cocycle is precisely the assumed $\mu$ cocycle evaluated at $T$, and its unit condition is normalization. The morphism equation for $R_ju$ is naturality of $\mu_{b,a}$. The functor laws hold componentwise because every $P(a)$ is a functor. Normalization gives $E_jR_j=1_{P(j)}$ on objects and morphisms.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 2 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text: For $X\in\widetilde P(j)$ define $(\eta_X)_a=\gamma^X_{a,1_j}$, with source $(R_jE_jX)_a$. Substituting $(c,b,a)=(b,a,1_j)$ in the family cocycle gives $\gamma^X_{b,a}P(b)(\eta_X)_a=(\eta_X)_{ba}\mu_{b,a,X_{1_j}}$, exactly the family-morphism equation. For a family morphism $t:X\to Y$, its equation at $(a,1_j)$ says $t_a(\eta_X)_a=(\eta_Y)_aP(a)t_{1_j}$, proving naturality in $X$. Inverting the components in these two equations gives a family morphism inverse and its naturality. Thus $\eta:R_jE_j\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ is a natural isomorphism. Together with $E_jR_j=1$ this proves the asserted equivalence, using the definition of equivalence in the statement. Notice $E_j\eta_X=1$ by $\gamma_{1,1}=1$.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 3 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text: Write $F_{a_0}=\widetilde P(a_0)$. For $a_0:j\to j_1$, define $(F_{a_0}X)_a=X_{aa_0}$, $(F_{a_0}t)_a=t_{aa_0}$, and $\gamma^{F_{a_0}X}_{b,a}=\gamma^X_{b,aa_0}$. The unit, cocycle and morphism equations are the original equations with last index $aa_0$, so these formulas give a functor. For $a_1:j_1\to j_2$, the component at $c:j_2\to k$ of $F_{a_1}F_{a_0}X$ is $X_{(ca_1)a_0}=X_{c(a_1a_0)}$; its structure maps and morphisms have the same equality of indices. Therefore $F_{a_1}F_{a_0}=F_{a_1a_0}$ and $F_1=1$ strictly.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 4 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text:
Set $\kappa_{a,X}=\gamma^X_{a,1_j}:P(a)E_jX\to E_kF_aX$ for $a:j\to k$. Naturality is the family-morphism equation at $(a,1_j)$, and the components are invertible by assumption. For $b:k\to l$, the cocycle at $(b,a,1_j)$ reads
$$\kappa_{b,F_aX}\,P(b)(\kappa_{a,X})=\kappa_{ba,X}\,\mu_{b,a,E_jX}.$$
The identity comparison is $\gamma_{1,1}=1$. These are exactly the required composition and identity coherences for $\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 5 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text:
For $z\in H(j)$ take $X_a=\alpha_k(H(a)z)$ and $\gamma_{b,a}=\theta_b(H(a)z)$. The source and target are $P(b)X_a$ and $X_{ba}$ because $H(b)H(a)=H(ba)$. The $\theta$ coherence for $(c,b)$, evaluated at $H(a)z$, gives
$$\theta_c(H(ba)z)\,P(c)(\theta_b(H(a)z))=\theta_{cb}(H(a)z)\,\mu_{c,b,\alpha_k(H(a)z)},$$
which is the family cocycle. The unit equation is $\theta_1=1$. For $u:z\to z'$ set $t_a=\alpha_k(H(a)u)$; naturality of $\theta_b$ gives the family-morphism equation. Functor laws are those of $H(a)$ and $\alpha_k$, so this defines $\widetilde\alpha_j$.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 6 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text: For $a_0:j\to j_1$ and $c:j_1\to k$, the components of $F_{a_0}\widetilde\alpha_j(z)$ and $\widetilde\alpha_{j_1}(H(a_0)z)$ are respectively $\alpha_k(H(ca_0)z)$ and $\alpha_k(H(c)H(a_0)z)$, hence equal. Their structure maps are both $\theta_b(H(ca_0)z)$, and their morphisms are equal by the same functor equality. Thus $\widetilde\alpha$ is strictly natural. Evaluation at $1_j$ gives $E_j\widetilde\alpha_j=\alpha_j$ on objects and morphisms, and $\kappa_{a,\widetilde\alpha_j(z)}=\theta_a(z)$ by the formula of the preceding step.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 7 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text: For the restriction clause, put $P_i=P(v(i))$ and $F_i=\widetilde P(v(i))$. Define $K(i)$ to have triples $Z=(X,T,\epsilon)$ with $X\in F_i$, $T\in P_i$, and an isomorphism $\epsilon:E_{v(i)}X\to T$. A morphism $Z\to Z'=(X',T',\epsilon')$ is a pair $(f,g)$ with $g\epsilon=\epsilon'E(f)$. Give it componentwise identities and composition: if $(f',g'):Z'\to Z''$, then $(g'g)\epsilon=g'\epsilon'E(f)=\epsilon''E(f'f)$. Category laws follow componentwise from [def-nagata-category]. The two component projections $q_i:K(i)\to F_i$ and $p_i:K(i)\to P_i$ are functors.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 8 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text:
For $r:i\to i'$ write $a=v(r)$ and define
$$K(r)(X,T,\epsilon)=(F_aX,P(a)T,P(a)(\epsilon)\kappa_{a,X}^{-1}),\qquad K(r)(f,g)=(F_af,P(a)g).$$
These are correctly typed. For a morphism $(f,g):Z\to Z'$, its image satisfies the required equation because
$$P(a)g\,P(a)\epsilon\,\kappa_{a,X}^{-1}=P(a)\epsilon'\,P(a)E(f)\,\kappa_{a,X}^{-1}=P(a)\epsilon'\,\kappa_{a,X'}^{-1}E(F_af).$$
The first equality uses $g\epsilon=\epsilon'E(f)$ and the second is naturality of $\kappa_a$. Identities and composition are preserved by the two functors acting on $f,g$.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 9 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text:
For composable $r,s$ put $a=v(r)$, $b=v(s)$. Applying $K(s)K(r)$ to the isomorphism of a triple gives
$$P(b)P(a)(\epsilon)\,P(b)(\kappa_{a,X}^{-1})\,\kappa_{b,F_aX}^{-1}=P(ba)(\epsilon)\,\kappa_{ba,X}^{-1}.$$
Indeed, on this restriction $P(b)P(a)=P(ba)$ and $\mu_{b,a}=1$, so the inverse of the displayed coherence in step 5 is $P(b)(\kappa_{a,X}^{-1})\kappa_{b,F_aX}^{-1}=\kappa_{ba,X}^{-1}$. The other two components and morphisms agree by strictness of $F$ and $P\circ v$. Identity arrows use $\kappa_1=1$. Thus $K$ is strict, and $q_{i'}K(r)=F_aq_i$, $p_{i'}K(r)=P(a)p_i$ by their component formulas.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 10 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text: The projection $q_i$ has quasi-inverse $S_i(X)=(X,E X,1)$, with $S_i(f)=(f,E f)$. It satisfies $q_iS_i=1$. At $Z=(X,T,\epsilon)$ the pair $(1_X,\epsilon):S_iq_iZ\to Z$ is a morphism because $\epsilon\cdot1=\epsilon E(1_X)$, with inverse $(1_X,\epsilon^{-1})$. Naturality for $(f,g)$ is exactly $g\epsilon=\epsilon'E(f)$. Hence $S_iq_i\cong1$, proving $q_i$ an equivalence directly, without a criterion involving full faithfulness or essential surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 11 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text: The projection $p_i$ has quasi-inverse $B_i(T)=(R_{v(i)}T,T,1)$, with $B_i(g)=(R_{v(i)}g,g)$; this is well-defined because $ER=1$, and $p_iB_i=1$. For $Z=(X,T,\epsilon)$ put $d_Z=\eta_X\circ R(\epsilon^{-1}):R(T)\to X$. Since $E\eta_X=1$ and $ER=1$, one has $E(d_Z)=\epsilon^{-1}$. Thus $(d_Z,1_T):B_ip_iZ\to Z$ satisfies $1_T=\epsilon E(d_Z)$ and is invertible, with inverse $(R(\epsilon)\eta_X^{-1},1_T)$. For $(f,g):Z\to Z'$, the relation $\epsilon'^{-1}g=E(f)\epsilon^{-1}$ and naturality of $\eta$ give $d_{Z'}R(g)=\eta_{X'}R(E(f)\epsilon^{-1})=f d_Z$. This proves the natural isomorphism $B_ip_i\cong1$, and hence the second projection is an equivalence.

source.place: Tag 004A, lemma-fibred-strict, contextual split-replacement source; step 12 is the agent-written direct verification for the explicit family model in this statement, not a quotation of the Stacks proof.

proof.text: Define $A_i:H(v(i))\to K(i)$ by $A_i(z)=(\widetilde\alpha_{v(i)}z,\alpha_{v(i)}z,1)$ and $A_i(u)=(\widetilde\alpha_{v(i)}u,\alpha_{v(i)}u)$. The equations $E\widetilde\alpha=\alpha$ verify the triple and morphism conditions. Along $r:i\to i'$, strict naturality of $\widetilde\alpha$ and the assumed strict naturality of $\alpha\circ v$ identify the first two components of $K(r)A_i$ with those of $A_{i'}H(v(r))$. The third component is $P(v(r))(1)\kappa_{v(r),\widetilde\alpha z}^{-1}=\theta_{v(r)}(z)^{-1}=1$, using precisely the identity-$\theta$ hypothesis on the restriction. The equality on morphisms follows from the first two components. Thus $A$ is strictly natural, and $qA=\widetilde\alpha\circ v$, $pA=\alpha\circ v$ as required.
